A solid, prismatic, circular shaft of uniform diameter d is subjected to a constant torque T = 1,000,000 N·mm over its full length L = 1,500 mm.
The material is 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25,939.8 MPa (N/mm²), assumed homogeneous and isotropic under small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior.
The design criterion is that the total angle of twist φ over the length L must not exceed φ_allow = 0.75° (converted to radians as π × 0.75 / 180).
The governing relation is φ = TL / (JG), where J = π d⁴ / 32 for a solid circular cross-section.
Solve the inequality TL / (JG) ≤ φ_allow for the minimum diameter d, working entirely in the N–mm–MPa unit system so that all intermediate quantities remain dimensionally consistent.
No transverse shear force or bending moment is present; the loading is purely torsional.
State the resulting minimum diameter d to the appropriate number of significant figures, and verify the solution by substituting d back into the twist equation to confirm φ ≤ φ_allow.
List any additional assumptions made (e.g., constant torque along the length, no stress concentration at ends, plane sections remain plane) in a brief note accompanying the result.
